div.span: This is the route uses for . Every part of the business follows it unless one is given a route of its own, which is done from the Matrix row rather than here.
This kind of request is not wired up to approvals yet, so you can write the route now but publishing waits until it is. Nothing here pretends to be protecting it in the meantime.

aside.p: The most specific always wins. Two routes covering exactly the same place are refused when you publish, so a request can never see two.

div.span: People are kept apart from the route. "HR lead" is worked out per part of the business from People & backups, so one shared route still gives each part its own approver.

span.t: Small amounts stay light; big ones bring in more people. Set the amount on each step.
Off — every step applies whatever the amount.

div.p: Amounts are compared in the money the request is in. Requests in different currencies are never added together.

span.span: Whoever prepared or sent it in never decides their own. Recommended.
Anybody named may decide, even their own work. Not recommended where money is involved.

label.span: Allow named exceptions to that rule

div.span: Where an exception has been arranged, the person may approve with a written reason. The decision is marked "an exception was used", kept in the trail, and whoever looks after this route is told. It never lets one person fill two seats of a joint approval.

select.option: The part of the business the request came from

div.span: Where a part of the business has nobody, the company-wide person covers it.
Each part of the business needs its own person — there is never a silent fall-back.

Naming somebody never gives them access and never creates an account. A person marked "Needs permission" can still be named — they just cannot open this kind of request until somebody gives them the access.

The person is worked out from the employee record of whoever the request is about. When a request covers many people at once, that means more than one person is asked — one per manager — so this is best kept for requests about a single person.
Save it to see who this reaches for the example on the right.
div.p: When the person holding a responsibility changes, new requests follow the change by themselves. Requests already under way keep the people they were given.
